A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Informed Meta-Learning and contain readable text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. The retained material can be matched reliably despite restructuring and renumbering.

before.justification: v2 reports original experiments on synthetic regression, weather prediction, CUB bird classification, and MNIST image completion, alongside analyses of training-task count, knowledge complexity, and spurious correlations.

after.justification: v3 retains original synthetic-regression, weather-prediction, and bird-classification results, together with the three supplementary analyses of learning and generalization.

M1.justification: The INP encoders, aggregation options, latent-variable decoder, ELBO objective, knowledge masking, and task-specific adaptations remain unchanged. Removing the MNIST evaluation does not establish a change to the proposed algorithm.

E1.justification: v3 removes the entire MNIST digit-informed image-completion task from v2 Appendix F.1, eliminating the evaluation of two-dimensional pixel regression. Synthetic one-dimensional regression, USCRN temperature extrapolation, and CUB bird classification remain.

E2.justification: The retained experiments preserve their NP baseline and informed/uninformed INP comparisons, including the same knowledge-format variants. Newly discussed prior methods are not evaluated as additional baselines; the MNIST experiment is removed as a whole.

E3.justification: The removed MNIST experiment takes away its pixelwise evaluation procedure, including reconstruction examples using 0, 16, 32, and 64 context pixels out of 784. Splits, training settings, metrics, and testing procedures for retained experiments are unchanged.

E4.justification: Removing Figure F.8 eliminates the qualitative analysis of how digit knowledge affects reconstruction as more pixels are observed. The training-task-count, knowledge-complexity, and spurious-correlation analyses in v2 F.2–F.4 remain in v3 A.6.1–A.6.3.

E5.justification: The caption of v3 Table A.3 newly specifies that standard errors were estimated with bootstrap; v2 Table F.3 only calls them estimated standard errors. Their numerical values remain identical, and no increase in experimental runs is reported.

E6.justification: v3 removes the MNIST log-likelihood curves and reconstruction findings in Figures F.7–F.8. Retained results are unchanged, including every numerical entry in Tables 2 and 3 and the appendix knowledge-complexity and correlation tables.

T1.justification: The formal framework, ELBO derivation, and predictive-uncertainty decomposition are retained. Shortening the delta-AUC explanation and reformatting or renumbering equations introduces no substantive mathematical change.

C1.justification: v3 qualifies its novelty claim by acknowledging earlier physics-specific combinations of informed ML and meta-learning, identifying its contribution as a generalized, representation-agnostic paradigm. The INP proof of concept and principal data-efficiency and robustness claims remain.

C2.justification: v3 adds an explanation distinguishing separately trainable PINNs from settings where knowledge integration itself must be learned. It omits v2's proposed use of uncertainty to formulate expert questions for active learning. The substantive underfitting, knowledge-overfitting, and spurious-correlation limitations remain.

D1.justification: v3 removes v2's statement that generated texts are released in supplementary materials and code will become available upon publication. Prompts, architectures, hyperparameters, and hardware details remain. This changes documented access information without establishing that resources were actually withdrawn.

R1.justification: The introduction and Appendix A.3 add substantive positioning against meta-learning for PINNs and metadata-conditioned meta-learning, citing works including HyperPINN, Meta-PDE, and TIML. These comparisons directly qualify novelty and explain the intended distinction between expert knowledge and metadata, substantially expanding the treatment of closely related approaches.

P1.justification: v3 extensively edits the main narrative, rewrites the contributions and closing discussion, replaces numbered method subsections with run-in headings, and merges the data-efficiency and distribution-shift subsections. Appendices A–F become A.1–A.6, and citations switch to numerical formatting.

P2.justification: v2 Figures 1 and 2 are combined into v3's three-panel Figure 1, while the two MNIST figures disappear. The title block, example-image table, correlation-table rules, and placements are revised. Most retained graphics preserve their plotted content.

improvement.justification: The added comparisons qualify novelty and clarify the central conceptual contribution, while the bootstrap disclosure improves statistical transparency. Retained main results and failure analyses preserve the principal evidence. These gains are limited by removal of the MNIST demonstration and the text/code release statement; v3 adds no new empirical validation.
